metadata.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models

problem.value: Existing scaling laws prioritize training compute budgets over inference efficiency budgets.

evidence.quote: The objective of the scaling laws from Hoffmann et al. ( 2022) is to determine how to best scale the dataset and model sizes for a particular training compute budget.

problem.value: Most high-performing language models rely on proprietary or undocumented training data.

evidence.quote: Unlike Chinchilla, PaLM, or GPT-3, we only use publicly available data, making our work compatible with open-sourcing, while most existing models rely on data which is either not publicly available or undocumented (e.g. "Books -2TB" or "Social media conversations").

contributions.value: Introduction of LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters trained exclusively on publicly available data.

evidence.quote: We introduce LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters.

task.value: Training large language models on massive text corpora for generative tasks.

evidence.quote: Large Languages Models (LLMs) trained on massive corpora of texts have shown their ability to perform new tasks from textual instructions or from a few examples (Brown et al., 2020).

limitations.value: Evaluation methods used are insufficient to fully understand model risks.

evidence.quote: While we have selected some of the standard benchmarks that are used by the language model community to indicate some of the issues with these models, these evaluations are not sufficient to fully understand the risks associated with these models.

limitations.value: Lack of control over the third-party PerspectiveAPI pipeline makes comparison difficult.

evidence.quote: We do not have control over the pipeline used by the third-party PerspectiveAPI, making comparison with previous models difficult.
Additionally, we observed like Chung et al. (2022) that finetuning these models on instructions lead to promising results, and we plan to further investigate this in future work.

future_work.value: Release larger models trained on larger pretraining corpora.

evidence.quote: Finally, we plan to release larger models trained on larger pretraining corpora in the future, since we have seen a constant improvement in performance as we were scaling.

ethics.value: Training models consumes significant energy and causes carbon emissions.

evidence.quote: The training of our models have consumed a massive quantity of energy, responsible for the emission of carbon dioxide.

claims.value: LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 on most benchmarks despite being much smaller.

evidence.quote: In particular, LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 (175B) on most benchmarks, and LLaMA-65B is competitive with the best models, Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B.

claims.value: LLaMA-65B is competitive with top large language models like Chinchilla and PaLM.

evidence.quote: At the higher-end of the scale, our 65B-parameter model is also competitive with the best large language models such as Chinchilla or PaLM-540B.
